clue.text: A sexually fluid work I see announced? Not necessarily

definitions.text: A sexually fluid work I see announced? Not necessarily

parts.note: short for bisexual
op. is short for opus, a work
taken as written

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word see is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced like see

explanation.surface: A gender-bending film or play hailed as a work about sexual fluidity, with a teasing question about whether it really is.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a biopic is a work about a life, and 'Not necessarily' admits its subject need not be bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: A biopic is a biographical film, a creative work whose subject may or may not have a fluid sexuality.

clue.text: Assimilate where fire may be lit, if not hot

indicators.note: not hot asks for the abbreviation for hot to be taken away

parts.note: a fire is lit in the fireplace's iron basket
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A fireside thought: something gets absorbed where a fire would be lit, unless it is not hot.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to combine into a whole, the same as absorbing or assimilating something.

clue.text: Solid support for Rhodes's statue?

parts.note: surface reading: firm backing for keeping Cecil Rhodes's contested Oxford statue
setter's reading: the literal stone base on which any statue stands

explanation.walkthrough: The Rhodes Must Fall campaign made 'support for the statue' sound political; the support meant is physical, the block underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue stands on a heavy base, the block that physically supports it.

clue.text: Seminars using slang endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: slang is colloquial language

explanation.surface: Academic meetings where the speakers keep using informal language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slang' is a noun in the surface but stands for the adjective describing informal speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquium is an academic conference or discussion meeting; this is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Nearby, very angry with oneself

definitions.meaning: first meaning: at the side of, close at hand
second meaning: the word placed with oneself gives the idiom for frantic with rage

explanation.surface: Someone furious with themselves, and someone else standing close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With oneself' is not self-reproach: the answer goes with the word oneself to make the idiom for being frantic or furious.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means next to, and the idiom 'beside oneself' means overwhelmed by emotion such as rage.

clue.text: One calls for the Army

parts.note: surface reading: a person who demands military intervention
setter's reading: military signals sounded on a brass instrument

explanation.walkthrough: 'Calls for' looks like demands; it means sounds signals, like reveille, for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: This brass instrument sounds military calls such as reveille and the Last Post to troops.

clue.text: Ashen, but work thus to get some colour

indicators.note: work as a verb means knead or shape, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Advice to someone pale: get out and work at acquiring a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in the sun is how people acquire a tan, which is getting some colour in the skin.

clue.text: Mike redubbed, turning up bearing another name

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top
bearing means carrying, so the words carry the letters inside them

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: An actor called Mike is renamed, popping up under a different name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redubbed' seems to say Mike gets a new name; it only holds the letters, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Derek is a man's given name, so it is just another name besides Mike.

clue.text: A consequence of bad hearing?

parts.note: surface reading: poor ears, deafness
setter's reading: a court hearing that went wrong has to be held again

explanation.walkthrough: Hearing looks like the sense of hearing, but it is a session in court; a flawed one leads to a second trial.
explanation.definitionFit: When a court case is unsound, through mistrial or bad procedure, the case is tried again in a fresh trial.

clue.text: Dangerous creature, a kestrel — ant is pulverised

indicators.note: pulverised means crushed to bits, so the letters are smashed and remade

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A bird of prey crushes an ant, a scene of a dangerous animal in action.
explanation.definitionFit: This venomous American snake, with a rattle on its tail, is a genuinely dangerous animal.

clue.text: Information on boy getting cheaper drug

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a boy's name; on places it after the first piece

explanation.surface: Someone has the lowdown on a lad who is getting a cheaper medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' simply means placed after. Gen (pronounced jen) is British slang for the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: A generic is a non-branded version of a medicine, sold at lower cost once the patent expires.

clue.text: One or two of these appear in the New Testament

definitions.text: One or two of these appear in the New Testament

parts.note: surface reading: a few people, as if characters in the Bible
setter's reading: the New Testament has the First and Second epistles to a city's people

explanation.walkthrough: 'One or two' reads as a vague handful; it is literally the numbers of the two epistles.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul wrote two letters to the Christians of Corinth, known as 1 and 2 Corinthians in the Bible.

clue.text: One's success is in the balance

definitions.text: One's success is in the balance

parts.note: surface reading: someone whose fate is uncertain, undecided

parts.words: One's success is in the balance
parts.note: setter's reading: a performer on a high wire succeeds only by keeping balance

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the balance' usually means undecided; here it is literal, as the performer's achievement lies in staying balanced.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus artiste walking a high wire stays up only by holding balance, so success depends on it.

clue.text: Idle head

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to laze about doing nothing
second meaning: British slang for the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' comes from rhyming slang, loaf of bread for head.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means laze about; as a noun it is slang for the head, from rhyming slang.

clue.text: Start one's piece, but not wait for the signal

parts.note: to start is to jump in surprise
piece is slang for a firearm

explanation.surface: A musician begins their solo too early, ignoring the conductor's cue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' suggests a piece of music; it is gangster slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from athletes leaving before the starting pistol, so it means acting prematurely without waiting.

clue.text: Mock battle in which the losers are the more decorated?

definitions.text: Mock battle in which the losers are the more decorated?

parts.words: the losers are the more decorated
parts.note: surface reading: defeated soldiers awarded more medals, a paradox
setter's reading: in this game players who are hit get splashed with colour

explanation.walkthrough: Decorated suggests medals; here it means covered in paint from pellets.
explanation.definitionFit: In this war game players fire pellets of dye at each other, so those hit end up splattered.

clue.text: Educational journey to old city, under £1K

indicators.note: in a down clue under means placed below, so what follows is set beneath the money word

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds
taken as written
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A study trip to an ancient city costing less than a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' means below, so the first two pieces sit beneath the money word.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional tour of European cities taken by young gentlemen to complete their education.

clue.text: Discharge online assignment?

parts.note: e- prefixes electronic, online things
a mission is an assigned task

explanation.surface: Someone is sacked over a task set on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: An emission is something given off or released, such as gas or fumes, a discharge.

clue.text: Old-fashioned medium broadcast modest aria

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A quaint old-style programme airs an unassuming operatic song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the radio scene so well it seems literal. Steam radio is a jokey British term for radio as against television.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam radio is a humorous name for the wireless, seen as an outdated means of communication beside television.

clue.text: Clean up US state briefly

indicators.note: briefly asks for a shortened form, so only the start of the name is kept

parts.note: a state in the north-west of the USA

explanation.surface: A call to tidy up an American state, as if in a political campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Wash. is the standard abbreviation for the state of Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash is to clean with water, and to wash up is to clean oneself or the dishes.

clue.text: Exams that French speakers often miss out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the last examinations of a degree course

definitions.text: that French speakers often miss out
definitions.meaning: second meaning: word-ending letters that are silent in French

explanation.surface: Tests that French students often skip.
explanation.walkthrough: French leaves many word-ending consonants unpronounced, as in petit or Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Finals are the exams at the end of a course, and also the closing letters of words.

clue.text: In novel, a short section an idiot misread

indicators.note: words misread come out jumbled, so these letters are taken in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
a passage is a brief extract of a text
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A fool has misinterpreted a brief extract in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In novel' looks like it frames the section, but 'novel' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: E. M. Forster's 1924 book about British India is one of the best-known English novels of the period.

clue.text: A barrier of stone

parts.note: taken as written
a gate bars a way through

explanation.surface: A stone wall or barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious stone, a variety of chalcedony.

clue.text: Hotel patron gets out uniform packed away

indicators.note: out means disordered or wrong, so the letters before it are rearranged
packed away means stowed inside, so one letter goes within the others

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel visitor goes out after the uniform is put away.
explanation.definitionFit: A person staying at a hotel is its guest, a paying customer.

clue.text: Test: cut back the one for me

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for cut from the end towards its start

parts.note: to axe is to cut
what belongs to me is mine

explanation.surface: A lab test in which a sample is trimmed back and the right one is chosen for me.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon follows the definition; 'cut back' is a verb phrase in the surface but a word plus its reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to inspect or test it closely, and to examine a student is to test them.

clue.text: Bewildered by how badly business is going

definitions.meaning: first meaning: puzzled, not knowing what to do
second meaning: a firm trading with costs above its income

explanation.surface: A business owner is baffled at how poorly the company is performing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at wits' end, and literally describes a company operating while its spending exceeds revenue.

clue.text: After exercise bring back fish and a sort of butter

parts.note: PE is physical education

indicators.note: to bring back is to return, so the fish word is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: a large sea fish

explanation.surface: After a workout, someone fetches a fish and a spread for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After exercise' places the PE first, since the rest comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanut butter is a common spread made from ground groundnuts, so the word is a kind of butter.

clue.text: Idlers said to go for the bright lights

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for idlers is judged by its sound

parts.note: lazers, those who laze, sound like the answer

explanation.surface: Layabouts are reported to be heading for the glamour of the bright lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bright lights' is the idiom for city glamour; here it is literal beams of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasers produce intense narrow beams of coherent light, so they are very bright lights.
